about: A weekly comedy series about a fictional golf four-ball and friends, made from quick-cut photo sketches. Recurring characters, running gags, continuity and character development, funny outcomes. John asked for it on 21 Nov 2026.
rules: Banter, never bullying: jokes are about golf, never anyone's looks, weight, age or anything personal.
Everyone gets a win sometimes; whoever gets ribbed this week can land the last laugh next week.
Characters are fictional, never based on or resembling a real person, never presented as real golfers or real stories.
One clear punchline per episode, a funny outcome, 8 to 12 seconds, cut on the 0.6-second beat.
No character leads two episodes in a row; Kev's reactions rotate.
Real figures only: if an episode mentions prices, only true, general statements (e.g. last season's models usually cost less) or real figures from data/.
No words, logos or brands in photos; keep each character's look identical.
About every other episode features one real tool naturally (see featureRule); the joke always comes first.

Dedicated shots (John, 26 Nov 2026): every character on screen in an episode gets a photo made for that episode's setting; re-use library photos only for the spare or when they truly match the scene (same place, season and lighting).

arcs.about: Gaz buys a new driver every few weeks; Kev keeps count. Payoff idea: Gaz finally finds his driver was fine all along, or buys last season's model for less and outdrives Kev. EP6 (spare): Gaz's 'new' last-season driver goes straight; Phil points out Gaz sold that exact driver in March (he bought his own old driver back).

Big Dave's creative scoring; Phil's props escalate (abacus, then calculator, then a referee's whistle, then the rule book). EP3: Phil brings the live scorecard as proof (the prop becomes our real tool). EP5: the props reach awards night (Phil's slideshow gives Dave 'Most Creative Scorecard').
Steady Steve keeps quietly winning with his 20-year-old irons while everyone else blames their kit. Payoff: the society cup.
Kev's own duffs get caught on camera; the group finally gets him back. EP4: Kev duffs it in front of Gaz and borrows Gaz's own excuse ('It's the shaft, mate').

December: the society Christmas dinner and awards (Dave's speech, Phil's 'honest scorecard' award, Gaz's gift is a driver). EP5: Phil runs the slideshow on our Society Awards kit; Dave expects Player of the Year and gets Most Creative Scorecard, and takes it as a compliment.
Phil is never wrong... until he is. Build it slowly (he's right in EP1 and EP3), then one day a rule or a price proves him wrong, and Kev frames it.

canon: EP1: Big Dave took six on a par 4 and called it a par. Phil offered him an abacus. Kev was in the background, trying not to laugh.
EP2: Gaz unboxed another new driver in the car park and sent his first drive into the trees. Kev: 'Must need a new driver.' Gaz: 'It's the shaft, mate.'
EP3: Big Dave claimed another par; Phil showed the live scorecard (six). Dave blamed the app. It's free, Dave.
EP4: Kev showed Gaz how it's done and took a divot the size of a doormat. Gaz: 'Must need a new driver, Kev.' Kev: 'It's the shaft, mate.' Gaz: 'At least mine went in the air.'
EP5: Society Christmas dinner. Dave announced Player of the Year; Phil's slideshow gave Big Dave 'Most Creative Scorecard' ('Take a bow'). Dave bowed and thanked his pencil.
EP6 (spare, may air out of order): Gaz's last-season driver finally went straight. Phil: he'd sold that exact driver in March.

big-dave: Takes every dig as a compliment (EP5: bows for 'Most Creative Scorecard'): oblivious, never wounded; keep that, it keeps the banter kind.
phil: Know-it-all (John, 21 Nov 2026): corrects everyone, quotes rules and stats, unrequested tips; deadpan delivery; usually right, which is the joke.
Props are his punchlines, and our tools are his favourite props (he 'knows' the price history, the real score, the rule).
Give him the occasional comeuppance: when Phil is wrong, it's an event (Kev's favourite day).
Props so far: abacus (EP1), live scorecard (EP3), awards slideshow (EP5). Still right every time: the 'phil-wrong' payoff gets stronger the longer it waits (aim for January).
steve: Not on screen yet and no photos of him exist. Plan his debut in January (steve-quiet-season arc, quiet win); ask John for his photos with that episode.
gaz: Kev's favourite target; gives as good as he gets.
EP4 gives him the last laugh (his comeback for EP2); EP6 gives him a straight drive. He's earning wins, keep him from being only the target.
kev: EP4 opens his comeuppance: when it's his turn he's no better, and reaches for Gaz's excuses. Use sparingly so Kev stays the likeable wind-up.

featureRule: Our tools are part of the world the characters live in. About every other episode, one real GolfPrice AI tool earns its place in the story: as Phil's prop, the proof, the twist or the punchline (EP3: the live scorecard proves Dave's six). The joke always comes first: if a tool would feel like an advert, leave it out that week. One tool per episode at most, shown truthfully (a real capture of the real page; demo data with the cast's names is fine, never a made-up interface or a feature we don't have), and the outro hands over to the same tool. Rotate tools so the series slowly shows off the whole site; deal tools and fun tools both count.
